John — thanks for the data and the PDF. High level response below; Kim and Aditya, paging you for details and the diagram.

Short answer: the least-risk pattern we recommend for your constraints is an internal active-active L4 termination in each AZ, with a pair of control-plane endpoints per region and an egress-proxy pair per tenant. Key considerations:

- Keep control-plane RPCs on the private subnet and route control-plane L4 VIPs via your internal fabric (no public NAT).
- Preserve session affinity on the L4 LB short-term (30s - 120s) for connections that carry warm KV cache pointers. We prefer sticky flows for the first 30s while the runtime populates local KVCaches.
- Implement a short soft-handoff: the runtime will accept traffic on both endpoints during a switchover but will prefer local KV filled state; we rely on a prefix-level cache replication (best-effort) to reduce cold misses.
- Observability: emit control_plane.role, control_plane.endpoint_id, kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.misses, kv_cache.populate.duration_ms, lb.connection_stickiness, and egress.proxy_id. We'll provide a suggested Splunk ingestion mapping.

I've attached a proposed termination diagram (proposed-termination-diagram.png) and a short KV-cache warmup proposal (kv-cache-warmup-proposal.md). Action items below.

Thanks John / Tessa — quick technical note from infra side.

- Cold start window: the 650ms spike aligns with a KV miss storm when the control-plane affinity switches AZs. Two mitigations: pre-warm (proactive population of hot prefixes on the DR cluster) and graceful connection draining with 1-2s of overlap where both endpoints accept reads but only the new leader accepts writes to control metadata.
- Replication approach: we don't currently ship synchronous prefix replication across AZs for large prefix sets (cost + write amplification), but we can do a best-effort async replication for the hottest N prefixes (operational parameter, default N=500). That reduces typical miss-storms to ~80-120ms for most workloads after first request fanout.
- LB choice: internal GCP/AWS NLB in TCP mode is fine. We recommend health-check TTLs of 5s and a stickiness TTL of 30s. Use BFD only if your fabric supports it; otherwise rely on platform health signals + short stickiness to avoid churn loops.

Instrumenting runbook items (suggested):
1) Pre-populate N=500 prefixes from the last 24h hot list across standby endpoints during deploys.
2) On switchover, set runtime to accept reads on both endpoints for 2s and delay write-only operations for 500ms to allow cache pointers to settle.
3) Alert: kv_cache.miss_rate > 3% sustained for 1m -> paging on-call and trigger a controlled rollback to previous control-plane endpoint.

I'll add a short appendix to the diagram describing the replication window and expected miss distribution.
